hypothesis: Within Mammalia, the fundamental structural agreement scored in a phenomic character matrix tracks an independently estimated genealogy more closely than it tracks habits of life: morphological distance among extant species correlates more strongly with phylogenetic distance than with ecological distance.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Using every extant species that is (i) a taxon in MorphoBank project 773 matrix X1766, (ii) placed as a tip on the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree, and (iii) matched to one EltonTraits 1.0 mammal row, compute pairwise morphological Hamming distance, phylogenetic distance, and ecological distance as specified in test_contract. Let r_p be the Spearman correlation of morphological distance with phylogenetic distance and r_e the Spearman correlation of morphological distance with ecological distance, both on the same complete-case pairs, and let delta = r_p - r_e. SUPPORTS if at least 20 taxa and at least 50 pairs enter the correlations, r_p >= 0.30, delta >= 0.15, and a one-sided permutation test of delta (4999 permutations, seed 20261101; p = (1 + number of permutations with delta >= observed delta) / 5000) gives p < 0.05.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if at least 20 taxa and at least 50 pairs enter, r_e >= 0.30, (r_e - r_p) >= 0.15, and the same permutation test applied to (r_e - r_p) gives p < 0.05. MIXED if at least 20 taxa and at least 50 pairs enter and neither the support rule nor the refute rule holds. INCONCLUSIVE with reason data-unavailable if the MorphoBank NEXUS file, the EltonTraits file, or the Open Tree induced subtree cannot be obtained or parsed. INCONCLUSIVE with reason underpowered if those files are obtained but fewer than 20 taxa or fewer than 50 complete-case pairs remain.
interpretation: Darwin's sentence is that unity of type — the fundamental agreement in structure among members of the same class, which he says is quite independent of their habits of life — is explained by unity of descent. The class tested is Mammalia, the class of his own examples (the same bones in a human hand, a bat wing, a porpoise fin, a horse leg). 'Fundamental agreement in structure' is every discrete phenomic character in the O'Leary et al. 2013 matrix (MorphoBank P773 / X1766), not a subset chosen after seeing which characters fit. That matrix includes teeth, proportions and other habit-tracking characters as well as the shared body plan, so ecology is given a real chance to win; using all characters is the conservative reading. 'Habits of life' are diet proportions, foraging-stratum category and activity time from EltonTraits 1.0, an external compilation. Body mass is not used: size is not a habit. 'Unity of descent' is path distance on the Open Tree synthetic tree, whose mammalian backbone is largely molecular, not the tree that was inferred from this same morphological matrix. Fossils in the matrix have no EltonTraits row and drop out. The claim is about every class; this test speaks only for the extant mammals that survive the match. A pass would not by itself cover birds or insects. Assessors named MorphoBank, Open Tree and GenBank. GenBank sequences are not re-downloaded; the synthetic tree is the molecular summary those assessors also named. Locus-by-locus concordance is not tested.

test_contract.expected_observation: Among extant mammals scored in the phenomic matrix, morphological distance rises with phylogenetic distance more than it rises with ecological distance: Spearman r of morphology with the Open Tree path is at least 0.30 and at least 0.15 higher than the Spearman r of morphology with diet, foraging stratum and activity, and that gap is larger than in 95 percent of label permutations.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Morphological distance tracks habits of life instead: the ecology correlation is at least 0.30 and at least 0.15 higher than the phylogenetic correlation, with the same permutation bar. That is the pattern Darwin attributed to conditions of existence rather than to unity of descent. If neither correlation clears the bar, the pre-registered contrast is mixed rather than a refutation, because a null is not positive evidence that habit explains structure.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A published discrete morphological matrix of mammalian structure, a phylogeny that was not built from that matrix, and a species-level table of diet, foraging stratum and activity compiled independently of both. The matrix must be the public MorphoBank P773 NEXUS (format=nexus, notes=0). Ecology must be the EltonTraits mammal table (diet percentages, ForStrat-Value, and the three activity columns), not body mass and not characters taken from the same matrix. Taxa must match on a binomial. Licence: the bytes have to be fetchable without a login.
test_contract.inference_method: Hamming distance is the fraction of characters on which both taxa have a scored state and the states differ. Missing and gap symbols are the FORMAT missing and gap symbols, plus empty. A polymorphic token {012} or (012) matches another token when their state sets intersect. Pairs compared on fewer than 100 characters are dropped. Phylogenetic distance is the number of edges on the path after unary nodes are collapsed; if at least half of the internal edges in the induced Newick carry a numeric length, the sum of those lengths is used instead and the choice is recorded. Ecological distance is Euclidean distance on the vector of 10 diet proportions (each Diet-* column divided by 100), a one-hot of ForStrat-Value using codes present in the matched taxa, and the three 0/1 activity columns. A taxon whose diet values sum to 0, or whose foraging or activity cells are blank, is dropped. Spearman correlations use the upper triangle of complete-case pairs. The permutation shuffles taxon labels of the morphological matrix only (rows and columns together) against fixed phylogenetic and ecological matrices. Thresholds are exactly those in pass_criterion and fail_criterion.

caveats: What was inspected before registration, and nothing else: the MorphoBank public project JSON for project 773 (description states 4,541 phenomic characters; publish_cc0 is 0; article DOI 10.1126/science.1229237; project DOI 10.7934/P773); a ranged read of the NEXUS download that showed the file starts with #NEXUS, reports NTAX=86, and lists the first six TAXLABELS; and bytes 0-1200 of MamFuncDat.txt (Content-Range reports the file is 579107 bytes; the header names the ten Diet-* columns, ForStrat-Value, three Activity-* columns and BodyMass-Value, and six data rows were in that byte range). No character-by-taxon matrix was parsed, no distance was computed, and no correlation was calculated. The 0.30 and 0.15 thresholds were chosen as a moderate correlation and a clear gap, not from those rows.

The phenomic matrix was assembled to study mammal phylogeny, so it is enriched for characters that vary among mammals in a hierarchical way. A correlation with an independent molecular tree is still the non-circular comparison the assessors asked for, but it is an easier test than a matrix assembled without phylogeny in view. The inclusion of adaptive characters works in the other direction.

EltonTraits was not named by the assessors. It is used because the claim's contrast is with habits of life and the assessors named no habits table. Diet, foraging stratum and activity time are the habits columns in the file that was header-checked.

One class is not every class. Mammals that lack an EltonTraits row or an Open Tree tip are absent. The synthetic tree has no branch support, so the permutation tests sampling of labels, not uncertainty of the tree.
